description: Builds organic structures from four-valent carbon, skeletal formulas, constitutional isomers, conformations, alkene geometry and aromatic electron delocalization.

related_resources.reason: Same-formula structural isomers, carbon chains and skeletons.
Single-bond rotation, staggered and eclipsed conformations.
Cyclic electron delocalization, energetic and structural aromaticity criteria.

historical_claims.anchor: The molecular formula C four H ten belongs both to a straight four-carbon chain

historical_claims.source_locator: Electron-delocalized cyclic aromatic systems, unlike odors.
Resonance drawings describe a delocalized electronic structure, not interconverting molecules.

authorship.scope: Original audio-first organic chemistry narration, scientific companion, sources, claims and comprehensive discovery metadata.

background: General valence and atomic bonding from chemistry foundations; geometry is developed in the lecture.
readiness_checks: Why can a molecular formula describe several constitutional isomers?
Why does rotating a single bond not normally change connectivity?
What evidence shows benzene is not a fixed ring of alternating isolated single and double bonds?
